statements.statement: Library presented its FY27 preliminary budget, a 3.5% increase over FY26, no staffing needs addressed.
Library's FY27 municipal appropriation requirement, the minimum to keep state certification (average of prior three years plus 2.5%).
Council on Aging is presenting a level-funded FY27 budget.
PAC expects $200,000 in revenue against its budget, leaving a deficit it wants covered from retained earnings; last year's draw was about $32,296 (also said 35,000).
PAC proposes new equipment/capital of $65,000 for FY27 (up from $30,000), mainly a server replacement of about $55,000.
PAC estimates Comcast franchise payments of about 38,000 a quarter, about 152,000 for the year, down from prior years.
Potential FY27 proposed Proposition 2 1/2 override is on the agenda; it will be the subject of the tri-board meeting March 10.

The school level-service budget is about $800,000 above what town meeting funded in the operating budget, and the restoration budget is another million on top; the $500,000 town meeting assigned is incorporated.

warnings.condition: if funding does not change / without town funding or alternative revenue
warnings.prediction: PAC would shift away from locally produced public and educational content, with no coverage of concerts, sports events and presentations, and might cut personnel or hours; the government channel would be prioritized.
An override failing would mean drastic cuts across the board.

warnings.about: school restoration budget bundled into one override question
warnings.condition: if the override is a single bundled restoration request
warnings.prediction: A restoration-only override request has a great chance of failing, with effects on students possibly as bad as 2012; the member urged splitting the requests.
If the override doesn't go through there will be hard consequences.
